extractions.metric: stated reason for the gain in these groups: greater representation of Biobank Japan and Genes & Health summary statistics

The Fig. 5b relative effect sizes are all within the UK Biobank and carry no Hispanic group.

extractions.metric: average variance explained on the liability scale by the PRS-CSx asthma score in the EUR target cohort, across 100 random splits
extractions.locator: Results, PRS performance across ancestries (Figure 5, Table S9)
extractions.excerpt_internal: The average R liability 2 in the EAS (0.053) and EUR (0.054) target cohorts approached the SNP-based heritability

extractions.metric: average variance explained on the liability scale by the PRS-CSx asthma score in the CSA target cohort, across 100 random splits
extractions.locator: Results, PRS performance across ancestries (Figure 5, Table S9)
extractions.excerpt_internal: while the prediction accuracies in the CSA (0.038) and AFR (0.014) target cohorts were lower

extractions.metric: average variance explained on the liability scale by the PRS-CSx asthma score in the AFR target cohort, across 100 random splits
extractions.locator: Results, PRS performance across ancestries (Figure 5, Table S9)
extractions.excerpt_internal: while the prediction accuracies in the CSA (0.038) and AFR (0.014) target cohorts were lower

extractions.metric: average variance explained on the liability scale by the PRS-CSx asthma score in the EAS target cohort, across 100 random splits
extractions.locator: Results, PRS performance across ancestries (Figure 5, Table S9)
extractions.excerpt_internal: The average R liability 2 in the EAS (0.053) and EUR (0.054) target cohorts approached the SNP-based heritability

extractions.metric: SNP-based heritability of asthma, the ceiling the liability-scale R2 values are compared against
extractions.excerpt_internal: approached the SNP-based heritability (h SNP 2), estimated to be 0.085 for asthma using the all-biobank meta-analysis

extractions.population: African, East Asian, European, Central and South Asian
extractions.metric: PRS target cohort sizes: AFR 849 cases / 5,190 controls; EAS 500/500; EUR 1,164/7,577; CSA 1,232/6,744
extractions.excerpt_internal: cases = 849 and controls = 5,190 for AFR; cases = 500 and controls = 500 for EAS; cases = 1,164 and controls = 7,577 for EUR; cases = 1,232 and controls = 6,744 for CSA

extractions.excerpt_internal: We evaluated the predictive performance of the PRS in 4 target cohorts: AFR ... CSA ... EAS ... and EUR ancestry individuals in UKBB

extractions.metric: qualitative finding on cross-biobank and cross-ancestry consistency of per-variant genetic effects
extractions.excerpt_internal: Despite the wide range in asthma prevalence among biobanks, we found largely consistent genetic effects across biobanks and ancestries

extractions.metric: meta-analysis scale: 153,763 cases and 1,647,022 controls across 22 biobanks; 179 loci, 49 not previously reported
extractions.excerpt_internal: a large-scale genome-wide association study of asthma (153,763 cases and 1,647,022 controls) via meta-analysis across 22 biobanks

extractions.metric: stated reasons estimates may differ across biobanks and ancestries: disease prevalence, environmental exposures, phenotype definitions
extractions.excerpt_internal: Estimates may differ across biobanks and ancestries given differences in disease prevalence, environmental exposures, phenotype definitions, and other factors

text_availability: Open access. Abstract and fullTextXML retrieved from PMC9903683. CSA is 'Central and South Asian' and is not South Asian-specific; GENARCH states that wherever the value appears.

title: Evaluating the use of blood pressure polygenic risk scores across race/ethnic background groups
population_labels_as_used: groups defined by self-reported race/ethnic background: Asian or Asian American (Asian), Black or African American/British (Black), Latino or Hispanic American (Hispanic/Latino), White or European American (White)

extractions.metric: grouping variable used: self-reported race/ethnic background, not a genetic-ancestry grouping
extractions.excerpt_internal: to train, assess, and validate PRSs in groups defined by self-reported race/ethnic background (Asian, Black, Hispanic/Latino, and White)

extractions.metric: residual variance, the denominator of the proportion-variance-explained statistic, was lowest in White and highest in Black participants, by up to 25% over White participants
extractions.locator: Results, characteristics of participants (Supplementary Figs. 1 and 2)
extractions.excerpt_internal: Residual variance, the denominator in the proportion variance explained statistic ... generally lowest in White ... highest in Black participants, by up to 25% over White

extractions.metric: estimated global continental genetic-ancestry proportions of the self-reported groups; stated qualitatively
extractions.excerpt_internal: Black participants are admixed with primarily African ancestries and some European ancestries, and Hispanic/Latino participants are admixed with substantial European, Amerindian, and African ancestries

extractions.metric: stated interpretation: stratified performance patterns were clearer in White and Hispanic backgrounds, suggesting a role for environmental and gene-environment effects
extractions.excerpt_internal: patterns were seen more clearly in White and Hispanic backgrounds than in Asian and Black backgrounds, again suggesting a role for more complex environmental and GxE effects

text_availability: Open access. Abstract and fullTextXML retrieved from PMC via Europe PMC. NOT used for a disease module: this study's groups are self-reported race/ethnicity categories and its 'Asian' group is not a South Asian-ancestry grouping, so it cannot support a South Asian-ancestry transferability metric without equating a census-style category with a genetic-ancestry group.
